item.title: Ireland South MEP calls for increased funding for Kerry Airport
item.description: An Ireland South MEP has called for increased funding for Kerry Aiport. Cynthia Ní Mhurchú, who’s on the EU’s Transport Committee, described the airport as vital to the regions economic prospects. A recent Airports Council International (ACI) report warned that European airports face a €360 billion infrastructure investment gap. item.title: Killarney travel agent advises those affected by Middle East conflict to wait for airlines to cancel flights
item.description: A Killarney travel agent is advising travellers affected by the widening Middle East conflict to wait for their airline to cancel their flight. Áine O'Donoghue of Torc Travel, Killarney says travellers should not cancel their flights, because they won't get a refund, and that they instead should wait for the airline to do so. item.title: Jessie Buckley Weekend launched to celebrate Kerry's own Hollywood star
item.description: Radio Kerry has teamed up with the National Tertiary Office (NTO) and partners MTU and Kerry College to celebrate our own Jessie Buckley. The Killarney actress has had a glittering awards season already this year, having won a Golden Globe, Critics' Choice Movie Award, BAFTA, IFTA, and Screen Actors Guild Award for her leading role in Hamnet. item.title: Kerry beaten by Meath
item.description: Kerry 2-2 Meath 2-12 Meath made the long journey to Kerry worthwhile as they claimed victory in Round 2 of the All-Ireland camogie championship, overcoming difficult, rain-soaked conditions to record a 2-12 to 2-2 win. The visitors made a blistering start, striking 1-3 inside the opening five minutes. They maintained the early momentum with two further points before Kerry eventually found their rhythm. item.title: Marine Nationale out of Cheltenham
item.description: Marine Nationale won't be defending his Queen Mother Champion Chase crown at Cheltenham next week. Trainer Barry Connell says the nine-year-old has a neck issue and has been entirely ruled out of the festival. Marine Nationale also won the Supreme Novices' Hurdle at Prestbury Park in 2023. item.title: Ireland make it two wins from two
item.description: The Irish men's hockey team have made it two wins from two in the World Cup Qualifiers in Chile. Lee Cole and Lewis Rowe scored two goals each in a 6-1 win over Korea. Ireland will have the chance to top their pool when they face Poland tomorrow afternoon. Advertisement

item.title: Man in critical condition after hit-and-run in Ardfert
item.description: A man is in a critical condition after a serious road traffic collision in Ardfert, whereby the driver failed to remain at the scene. This collision occurred last night and Gardaí have issued an appeal for witnesses. This collision involved a car and a pedestrian and it happened in the Tubrid More area of Ardfert around 9.20 last night. item.title: Councillor airs frustration at local authority lack of action to protect Kerry’s coastlines
item.description: A South Kerry councillor has aired his frustration at what he describes as the local authority's lack of action on the coastal crisis. Fianna Fáil’s Tommy Cahill was speaking at recent meeting of Kerry County Council. He says he’s shocked and angered that no applications have been submitted to the OPW for coastal protection and flood relief works at Rossbeigh or Cromane. item.title: England make nine changes
item.description: England head coach Steve Borthwick has made nine changes on the back of their hammering by Ireland. Fin Smith, in his first start since the autumn, replaces George Ford at fly-half in a new backline for Saturday's trip to Italy in the Six Nations. Advertisement
